dimension_policy.final_correctness: 0-2 on every item; full ambiguity, impossibility, and query-plan answers count as complete; conditional induction is not required to be unrestrictedly unique.

meaningful_alternatives.induction_policy: Task-required unrestricted ambiguity can receive full credit without a catalog of named alternatives; additional named alternatives are not automatically extra credit.

discriminating_test.operational_interpretation: A separating query with differing predictions, decisive proof, or complete finite candidate/event verification earns 2. Fitting supplied examples without a concrete separating comparison earns 1. Plans are not reported as executions.

dimension_policy.aggregation: Dimensions remain separate; no weighted composite.

Q04.method: Assessor-written enumeration of all 64 subsets of six swap pairs, BFS from 1234, and transition-by-transition validation of every submitted path.

Q07.method: Assessor-written enumeration of 10 hidden values, 15 visible positions, and 9 genuinely different replacements, checking both equations in every row.

Q08.method: Assessor-written enumeration of all 4096 strings and nine overlapping windows, independently cross-checked by a last-bit/current-run-length recurrence that rejects runs of length four.

independent_verification.provenance: These checks were executed by the assessor during this assessment. They authenticate results, not solver execution histories.

cost_measurement.normalization: For each item, canonical JSON is json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2). Canonical word count uses whitespace-delimited nonempty tokens. String-content words count whitespace-delimited tokens in all string leaf values under answer/evidence/next_test, excluding id/status and JSON field names. Numeric leaf values are not counted as string-content words. Arm totals sum per-item counts.
cost_measurement.missing_measurement_policy: Unavailable; not estimated from prose or reported as zero.

limitations: Twelve fixed puzzles and one visible response per label provide a small diagnostic with ceiling effects, not an estimate of general puzzle performance, robustness, or causal treatment effects.

Only response labels are anonymized. Wording, structure, lengths, and claimed checking remain visible and may reveal stylistic or treatment cues. The assessor also sees the rubric and gold answers; this is partial blinding, not double blinding.
No arm mapping, source skill, source libraries, other runs, or other assessments were inspected. No private reasoning was requested, inferred, or scored.

Solver execution traces and run metadata were not supplied. Claimed BFS/enumeration executions are unauthenticated, not established fabrications. Assessor verification confirms the mathematical results, not whether a solver executed its claimed procedure.
Calibration scores reflect visible answer/status alignment; the absence of evidence of fabrication is not evidence that execution claims were authenticated.

Words and characters are reproducible measurements of normalized visible response content. Actual delivered serialization, model token usage, runtime, calls, retrieval, retries, resets, and complete delivered input sizes are unavailable.

The secondary test scores depend on an explicit operational reading of the rubric: checking supplied induction examples is partial, while a separating test or complete finite candidate/event verification earns full credit. This affects one point of between-label separation and does not affect correctness or calibration.
All responses use the intended Q01/Q02 mechanisms. Alternative-simple-mechanism correctness credit was available but was not needed, so no simplicity judgment affects the comparison.
One assessor and coarse 0-2 dimensions cannot resolve small qualitative differences; no weighted composite or general winner is inferred.
material_differences: R68 Q01 specifies an unexecuted hollow-ring test with predictions 16 for all exposed sides and 12 for exterior-only boundary. This gains one secondary discriminating-test point over R17/R42; all have equally complete conditional answers.
R42 Q04 uses a different valid shortest sequence; independent transition checks confirm it is equally correct.
R17 Q12 uses a different optimal partition; both displayed partition choices achieve totals 13 and 14.
The prose and output structures vary in length. No additional correctness, mechanism, alternatives, or calibration credit is awarded for verbosity or claimed computation.
